standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic household budget connection task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The task sheet provides a fictional budget template for the persona - a made-up monthly income figure and a short list of made-up round-number expense categories such as rent, groceries, and transportation - and the learner matches each expense category to the specific calendar block (work, sleep, errands, or rest) it most affects, then checks whether the persona's invented work-block hours could plausibly produce the invented income figure.
materials: learner-local: the persona's one-month calendar skeleton from the previous lesson

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l02-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l02-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l02-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l02-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Which single budget category most changed how you look at one of the persona's calendar blocks, and why?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u06-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Budget-to-calendar linkage: Each budget category is matched to a specific calendar block with a stated reason. | Income and hours plausibility check: Math shown correctly connects a chosen hourly wage and the persona's work-block hours to a plausible monthly total near $1,800. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner invent one unexpected fictional expense (such as a $120 car repair) for the persona and rewrite the budget template to absorb it by trimming exactly one other category, explaining their choice in writing.

resources.title: household budget connection worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The task sheet provides a fictional budget template for the persona - a made-up monthly income figure and a short list of made-up round-number expense categories such as rent, groceries, and transportation - and the learner matches each expense category to the specific calendar block (work, sleep, errands, or rest) it most affects, then checks whether the persona's invented work-block hours could plausibly produce the invented income figure.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact household budget connection decision or action.

Model move 2: Read the provided fictional budget template for your persona: a made-up monthly income of $1,800, and made-up round-number monthly expenses of $650 for rent, $100 for utilities, $300 for groceries, $150 for transportation, $200 for savings, and $200 for flexible spending.
Model move 3: Match each budget category to the calendar block from the previous lesson that it connects to most directly.

Model check: Budget-to-calendar linkage: Each budget category is matched to a specific calendar block with a stated reason. | Income and hours plausibility check: Math shown correctly connects a chosen hourly wage and the persona's work-block hours to a plausible monthly total near $1,800.

resources.title: household budget connection action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for household budget connection.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: household budget connection coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The task sheet provides a fictional budget template for the persona - a made-up monthly income figure and a short list of made-up round-number expense categories such as rent, groceries, and transportation - and the learner matches each expense category to the specific calendar block (work, sleep, errands, or rest) it most affects, then checks whether the persona's invented work-block hours could plausibly produce the invented income figure.

Coach direction: Read the provided fictional budget template for your persona: a made-up monthly income of $1,800, and made-up round-number monthly expenses of $650 for rent, $100 for utilities, $300 for groceries, $150 for transportation, $200 for savings, and $200 for flexible spending.
Learner prompt: I read every category in the persona's fictional budget template before starting.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: household budget connection complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Match each budget category to the calendar block from the previous lesson that it connects to most directly.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I matched the rent and utilities categories to the persona's sleep/home block.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I matched the transportation category to the persona's errands or work block, whichever fits the persona's month better.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I matched the savings category to a specific recurring moment in the persona's month rather than leaving it unconnected.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: household budget connection minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Which single budget category most changed how you look at one of the persona's calendar blocks, and why?

Success checks: Budget-to-calendar linkage: Each budget category is matched to a specific calendar block with a stated reason. | Income and hours plausibility check: Math shown correctly connects a chosen hourly wage and the persona's work-block hours to a plausible monthly total near $1,800.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: household budget connection supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g8-u06-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional household budget connection condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Budget-to-calendar linkage: Each budget category is matched to a specific calendar block with a stated reason. | Income and hours plausibility check: Math shown correctly connects a chosen hourly wage and the persona's work-block hours to a plausible monthly total near $1,800..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: household budget connection — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the household budget connection task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.

retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
